title: DentalOS
summary: The administrative workflow of a fictional dental clinic, Clínica Brisa: a portal for patients and a panel for the front desk, clinicians and management, in 16 modules. Frontend only, with synthetic data: it sends no messages, makes no calls and charges nothing.

facts.v: Synthetic, with a fixed sample clock

tldr.v: In a clinic, an appointment rescheduled over WhatsApp loses its reminder, an orthodontic check-up never gets booked and an estimate gets no answer.
Every visit has a next step: appointments that change without getting lost, reminders that are voided and rescheduled, a waitlist and rule-bound recall campaigns.
A local demo with no backend. It is not clinical software: the breadth of the demo is not a promise of scope.

p: A demo to show a general dentistry and orthodontics clinic how it could organise its administrative workflow. Clínica Brisa, its patients and its clinicians are made up, and patients are identified by sample IDs (P-001…), never by ID documents.
list: Patient or responsible adult: books on a calendar with the free slots, sees their appointments and estimates, and tries a simulated WhatsApp chat and phone call. There is an educational section for children, with games.
Front desk: schedule by day, week or clinician, message inbox, people and families, waitlist and reminders.
Clinician: an odontogram with five surfaces per tooth and orthodontic follow-up.
Management: estimates with a fictional till, reports that show their denominator, campaigns and a simulator with 12 scenarios.
The role picker is a view for the demo, not a login.

reschedule.h: The idea: every visit has a next step
p: The demo's 90-second script shows the most common and most fragile case: a patient who changes their appointment over WhatsApp.
reschedule.title: Rescheduling without losing the appointment

steps.d: «I want to change my appointment»: the chat recognises the intent with local rules, no AI.
If the chosen time is taken, the original appointment stands.
Clinician, chair, site, duration, minimum notice and that it isn't in the past.
Sees before and after. Appointment A-0012 becomes version 2, with the same ID.
The version 1 reminder is voided and the version 2 one is scheduled.
A-0012 v2 shows up in the panel, with its outbox and its audit trail.

reschedule.caption: It all happens in the browser: no message is really sent.

p: The rest of the demo follows the same idea:
list: Waitlist: when a slot frees up, it is offered to someone waiting for a compatible one.
Estimates: a minor can't accept one, and neither can an adult who isn't their guardian. Accepting is not paying.
Recall campaigns: segments computed from the state (pending check-ups, unanswered estimates), with opt-out, exclusions and a cap of 2 messages in 30 days per person.
Economics before launch: contribution and break-even; if a figure is missing, the campaign stays a draft.
Projected, simulated and observed results, kept apart: booking is not treating or charging, and attribution does not prove causation.

p: A React SPA built with Vite into static files, with its own hash router and store. Screens don't modify the state: they send commands to a pure domain layer, with no React.

diagram.title: One state, changed by commands
diagram.caption: No backend, database, AI, authentication, messages, calls, payments or analytics. CI publishes it on GitHub Pages.

ls.label: localStorage
ls.note: Versioned and validated on hydration. If it is damaged the demo says so and offers a restore; with no access it runs in memory; if another tab changes it, it warns.

domain.label: Pure domain
domain.note: Each command is applied to a copy of the state: if it fails, the whole copy is thrown away.

clock.label: Clock
clock.note: An injected sample clock: ESLint forbids Date.now and Math.random, so the demo plays out the same every time.

outbox.label: Outbox
outbox.note: Reminders, offers and campaigns keyed by appointment, version and type: they don't duplicate and none leaves the browser.

p: This is the central technical piece: every change is atomic and idempotent. A double click doesn't book twice and an error leaves nothing half done.

seq.title: From the click to the saved state
seq.caption: If the handler fails with a domain error (PASADO, SERVICIO_INCOMPATIBLE…), the copy is thrown away and the original state stays intact. It is a local transaction, not a distributed guarantee.

p: A health demo has to be discreet even when its data is made up. The limits live in the build and the linter, not only in the docs.

items.d: The build's CSP declares connect-src 'none', frame-src 'none' and form-action 'none', and ESLint forbids fetch.
ESLint forbids dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and the saved state is structurally validated before it is used.
Sample IDs instead of ID documents. No photos, X-rays, maps, embeds, CDNs or tracking; fonts and icons are local.
Switching role changes the screen, not the permissions: there is no authentication and it is not presented as security.
Templates carry no treatments, diagnoses or amounts, and a rule rejects alarmist tone and clinical detail.
No diagnosis, triage or treatment advice, and no microphone. The dental artwork is marked as pending review by a dentist.

items.why: It is a local demo: the build's CSP closes connections and an ESLint rule forbids fetch.
An injectable clock and no Date.now or Math.random; the games use a seed. The same demo tells the same story every time.
Atomic, idempotent commands keyed by commandId, applied to a copy of the state, with an outbox and an audit trail, and no third-party router or state library.
A versioned, validated envelope; if damaged, a warning plus restore or download a copy; with no access or no quota, memory mode. Resetting only clears its own namespace.
Each requirement has an ID, source, scenario and evidence, and a specified requirement doesn't count as done until there is evidence. One PR per batch.
The chat and the management assistant are rules: the figures come from the state and there are no canned answers that could contradict it.

p: Before publishing, CI runs lint, typecheck, unit tests, the build and the e2e suite. The repo documents an intermittent e2e failure, a race with a game's clock, that was found and fixed.

items.d: Unit: domain, campaigns, games, WCAG contrast and SVG artwork
Playwright, listed in 13 files, not run

quality.note: I ran the unit tests with Vitest on 28/10/2026: 190 green, in 6 files. I listed the 93 e2e tests that day with Playwright's list mode, in 13 files; I didn't run them. I counted the 16 modules and the 59 command types in the code.

status.h: Status and what I don't claim
list: Pre-sales demo. Clínica Brisa, its patients and its clinicians are fictional.
It is not clinical software or a medical record, no clinic uses it, and the odontogram has no medical precision.
It doesn't send WhatsApp messages or make calls, and the assistants are rules, not AI.
Roles are views: there is no authentication or access control.
It has no price and no defined business model.
Batches 1 to 6 of 10 are closed. Pending: appointment code and QR, call sounds, a guide by role, full QA and measured performance.
Not tested with a real screen reader or in Safari or Firefox. I listed the e2e tests, but didn't run them.
